name.full: Orion Fenwick of the Hive Choir

epithet: who remembered what no one had asked to be remembered
mannerisms: measures the height of doorframes by habit
has a notebook nobody is allowed to read
collects the names of streets they will not return to
voice: precise as cut glass and just as hard to argue with
aspiration: to set the record straight before they go
fear: the last person walking out without saying anything
gift: they keep their word in conditions that release others from theirs
wound: a parent who left and called it work
secret: that they have been carrying a body, metaphorically, for decades

threads.desc: who left without an argument, and whose silence {name} still rehearses answers to
who left a letter that {name} has not finished reading
who has been chasing the same prize for so long that the chase is the friendship

backstory.origin: Orion was born in The Undercroft, of the Hive Choir, the last child of a baker and a clerk.
backstory.weight: The family is built on a series of leavings. Two generations back, a father vanished into work and never quite returned. Orion's parent learned to expect this kind of departure, and so did Orion.
backstory.fracture: It was their grandmother's last week. Orion was twenty-eight, and they understood, suddenly and with no warning, that nobody else was going to carry what she had carried. They have been carrying it since.
backstory.between: They drifted through a stretch of years that produced fewer stories than the decade before. Orion grew quieter, then briefly louder, then quieter again. There was a project — a letter to the council that took years — that almost worked.
backstory.present: These days, Orion can be found at the same café most mornings. They have a stack of unanswered letters that they will not throw away, and a habit of lighting one candle before breakfast that even their oldest friends find slightly strange.
